title: Forward Cargo Door Surround Corner — Gusset Replacement Repair

issue.reason: Original issue of the corner gusset replacement repair for the forward cargo door surround.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Replacement of a damaged corner gusset at the forward cargo door cut-out, with separate allowable damage limits for the 40 mm and the 55 mm corner radius standards.

sections.purpose: This repair replaces a cracked or impact-damaged corner gusset at the forward cargo door cut-out and restores the local load path into the door surround stringer.
sections.damage_assessment: Identify the corner radius standard of the aircraft before any limit is applied, because the 40 mm and the 55 mm standards have different allowable damage boundaries and the wrong boundary will pass damage that is not acceptable. Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection and by an eddy current sweep of the corner arc and of the first fastener row on each side of it. Damage on the gusset itself is covered by this repair. Damage that has propagated into the cut-out radius, into the intercostal, or into the stringer run-out is outside the scope and needs an engineering assessment. Record the corner position, the arc angle at which the damage starts and the damage length, and photograph the corner before removal.
sections.repair_procedure: Put the cargo door in the maintenance position and make it safe against inadvertent operation. Remove the sill panel and the local lining panels to expose the corner. Drill out the fasteners that attach the gusset D5321130372071, working from the arc centre outwards, and remove the gusset. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the exposed cut-out radius over the full arc and an eddy current inspection of every open hole. Where a hole is elongated beyond the limit on repair drawing RD-53-21-13-901, ream it to the oversize dimension shown and use the oversize fastener from the same drawing. Offer the replacement gusset and check the fit against the corner radius; a gusset for the 55 mm standard will not seat on a 40 mm corner and must not be forced. Where the corner has already been repaired once, or where the crack reaches the second fastener row, use the double-gusset arrangement on sheet 2 of the repair drawing, which adds a second plate on the inner face and a further fastener row inboard of the arc. Install the gusset or gussets wet with sealant using bolts AES495354-07 and anchor nuts AES462858-1A, torqued in the sequence given on the drawing. Restore the protective treatment and the sealant fillet at the corner. Install the lining and the sill panel and do the cargo door operational test before the aircraft is released.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the repaired corner at every C-check and an eddy current inspection of the corner arc every 6 000 flight cycles until two consecutive inspections are clear. Where an oversize fastener has been used, the eddy current inspection remains at 6 000 flight cycles for the life of the repair. Not more than two corners of one door surround may carry this repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the corner radius standard of the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: On the 40 mm corner standard, gusset cracks up to 15 mm that do not reach the cut-out radius. On the 55 mm corner standard, gusset cracks up to 22 mm under the same condition. The double-gusset arrangement extends both figures by 8 mm. Not more than two corners per door surround.

repair_drawings.title: Corner gusset replacement, forward cargo door surround

type_data.fastener_pattern: Twenty-eight bolts around the gusset perimeter, 22 mm pitch, 16 mm edge distance, with oversize positions marked on sheet 2
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit where standard fasteners are used; where an oversize fastener is used the eddy current inspection remains at 6 000 flight cycles for the life of the repair.

title: Forward Cargo Door Surround Corner — Gusset Replacement Repair

issue.reason: Repair variant made a recorded output and the double-gusset arrangement declared incompatible with the corner reinforcement, which the single-gusset arrangement clears.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Replacement of a damaged corner gusset at the forward cargo door cut-out, with separate allowable damage limits for the 40 mm and the 55 mm corner radius standards and a recorded variant that decides eligibility for the corner reinforcement.

sections.purpose: This repair replaces a cracked or impact-damaged corner gusset at the forward cargo door cut-out and restores the local load path into the door surround stringer.
sections.damage_assessment: Identify the corner radius standard of the aircraft before any limit is applied, because the 40 mm and the 55 mm standards have different allowable damage boundaries and the wrong boundary will pass damage that is not acceptable. Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection and by an eddy current sweep of the corner arc and of the first fastener row on each side of it. Damage on the gusset itself is covered by this repair. Damage that has propagated into the cut-out radius, into the intercostal, or into the stringer run-out is outside the scope and needs an engineering assessment. Record the corner position, the arc angle at which the damage starts and the damage length, and photograph the corner before removal.
sections.repair_procedure: Put the cargo door in the maintenance position and make it safe against inadvertent operation. Remove the sill panel and the local lining panels to expose the corner. Drill out the fasteners that attach the gusset D5321130372071, working from the arc centre outwards, and remove the gusset. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the exposed cut-out radius over the full arc and an eddy current inspection of every open hole. Where a hole is elongated beyond the limit on repair drawing RD-53-21-13-901, ream it to the oversize dimension shown and use the oversize fastener from the same drawing. Offer the replacement gusset and check the fit against the corner radius; a gusset for the 55 mm standard will not seat on a 40 mm corner and must not be forced. Where the corner has already been repaired once, or where the crack reaches the second fastener row, use the double-gusset arrangement on sheet 2 of the repair drawing, which adds a second plate on the inner face and a further fastener row inboard of the arc. Install the gusset or gussets wet with sealant using bolts AES495354-07 and anchor nuts AES462858-1A, torqued in the sequence given on the drawing. Restore the protective treatment and the sealant fillet at the corner. Enter the arrangement used, single or double gusset, on the aircraft structural record sheet; it is the record that later decides whether the corner can take the reinforcement. Install the lining and the sill panel and do the cargo door operational test before the aircraft is released.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the repaired corner at every C-check and an eddy current inspection of the corner arc every 6 000 flight cycles until two consecutive inspections are clear. Where an oversize fastener has been used, the eddy current inspection remains at 6 000 flight cycles for the life of the repair. A corner carrying the single-gusset arrangement may take the reinforced corner fitting of MOD-111071 without further work, because the machined cut-out profile of that fitting clears the single-gusset fastener pattern. A corner carrying the double-gusset arrangement may not: the inboard row of the second plate falls inside the machined profile, and such a corner is outside the effectivity of Service Bulletin CRN-53-1021 until a separate scheme has been agreed with the repair office. Not more than two corners of one door surround may carry this repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the corner radius standard of the aircraft and the arrangement used.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: On the 40 mm corner standard, gusset cracks up to 15 mm that do not reach the cut-out radius. On the 55 mm corner standard, gusset cracks up to 22 mm under the same condition. The double-gusset arrangement extends both figures by 8 mm but makes the corner ineligible for the reinforced fitting. Not more than two corners per door surround.
